question: Why might a design pass in Verilator but fail in a 4-state simulator such as Questa or Icarus?
rubric: Explains that Verilator is 2-state, so X and Z become 0 or 1
Says uninitialised registers (missing resets) show up as X only in 4-state simulators
Mentions X-propagation differences (X-optimism or pessimism in if/case statements)
Mentions scheduling or race differences (blocking assignments, combinational loops settling)
Recommends running both kinds of simulator or Verilator's X-initialisation randomisation
